qa_pair.question: Rank Nextflow lint, preview with DAG, stub-run, and a small real fixture by what each can prove. Which is the first level that proves a process command actually executed?
qa_pair.answer: Lint proves syntax/style diagnostics; preview evaluates workflow construction and renders a DAG while skipping processes; stub-run executes declared stub bodies instead of real process scripts; a small real fixture executes actual process commands. The small real fixture is the first listed level that proves real process commands ran.

qa_pair.question: A pipeline is resumed after changing a script in bin, changing a process script, and changing only an input file timestamp. Explain which changes can invalidate cached tasks and how deep caching changes file comparison.
qa_pair.answer: Executable scripts in bin are part of task identity, so changing one can invalidate tasks that use it. A changed process script can also invalidate its task. Standard file caching uses path, size, and modification time; deep caching hashes contents, so a timestamp-only change does not invalidate under deep caching.

qa_pair.question: Legacy and strict parsers receive profiles standard,cloud in that command-line order, but the profiles were declared in the opposite order. Which order is applied by each parser?
qa_pair.answer: The legacy parser applies profiles in configuration declaration order regardless of command-line order. The strict parser applies them in command-line order: standard, then cloud.

qa_pair.question: How do typed workflows and typed processes divide dataflow types from ordinary value types, and which component reports a take/emit mismatch before execution?
qa_pair.answer: Typed workflows model asynchronous values as Channel<T> or Value<T>, whose elements use ordinary standard types. Typed process inputs/outputs use ordinary standard types and exclude Channel/Value annotations. The Nextflow language server validates workflow take/emit contracts before execution.

qa_pair.question: An installed registry module was edited locally. Which metadata records its installed version, how does listing expose the edit, and what removal option preserves files while dropping registry tracking?
qa_pair.answer: The module directory's .module-info records installed version/integrity metadata. nextflow module list reports integrity status and local modification. nextflow module remove -keep-files removes .module-info while retaining module files.

qa_pair.question: Why can a symlinked process input work on the host but fail in a Nextflow container, and what image-level commands must be available for execution and metrics?
qa_pair.answer: Nextflow mounts task inputs, but a symlink target outside the symlink directory tree may not be mounted and becomes inaccessible. The image needs Bash 3 or newer at /bin/bash as entrypoint, plus ps and metric helpers including awk, date, grep, sed, tail, and tee.

qa_pair.question: Distinguish execution log, report, trace, timeline, DAG, and lineage as evidence. Which carry task resource metrics, and which can exist without executing tasks?
qa_pair.answer: The log indexes runs/tasks; the HTML report summarizes run, resources, and tasks; trace is tabular per-task timing/resource data; timeline visualizes task timing; DAG shows workflow structure; lineage records provenance when enabled. Report, trace, and timeline carry task execution/resource evidence. A preview DAG can exist without task execution.

qa_pair.question: Under strict syntax, how should custom classes, top-level executable statements, untyped variables, and CLI boolean-looking legacy params be migrated?
qa_pair.answer: Move custom classes to lib or replace helpers with standalone functions; move executable top-level statements into the entry workflow; declare variables with def or supported local annotations; and do not rely on legacy CLI coercion—treat values as strings or use a typed params block.

qa_pair.question: Compare Nextflow Conda package specs, environment YAML, explicit/lock files, and containers as task environments. Which two most directly freeze artifacts, and what portability caveat remains?
qa_pair.answer: Package specs and environment YAML normally require solving; explicit/lock files enumerate resolved package artifacts and may include hashes; containers package a filesystem behind an image reference. Explicit/lock files and digest-pinned container images freeze artifacts most directly, but remain platform-specific and require compatible runtimes.

qa_pair.question: In nextflow run, distinguish Nextflow options from pipeline parameters, including hyphen forms. How is a parameter named input-file passed?
qa_pair.answer: Nextflow runtime options use a single hyphen; pipeline parameters use a double hyphen and populate params. The parameter is passed as --input-file value, following the project invocation as documented.
